purpose: understand users' real behavior, goals and difficulties through research, and turn it into findings the design can use
entry_criteria: A user group and research question are defined
Consent and privacy rules are agreed
procedure: Write the research questions and choose methods that fit them: interviews, observation, diary study, survey or usability test.
Recruit participants who match the real user groups, including less technical and assistive-technology users.
Get consent, explain how data is used and stored, and keep personal data to the minimum needed.
Run the sessions, record what people did and said, and avoid leading questions.
Analyze across participants, and report patterns with the number of people who showed each one.
Share findings as problems and opportunities with evidence, and note the limits of the sample.
acceptance_criteria: Findings state how many people showed each pattern
Limits of the sample are stated

validation.check: check each participant has a consent record and each finding shows a count
check recruitment included at least one participant using assistive technology

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: Eight users are observed filing an expense claim. Five miss the receipt upload button; the report gives the count of five of eight, notes that all were in one department, and recommends testing with others.
